# Trame · Generations

*The graph in force on 3 November 2026, generated by `trame build` from `src/generations.ts`. This document follows the code: to change it, change the code.*

> **9 acceptance criteria passed out of 9**

## Requirement

<a id="AcceptCandidate"></a>

### Accept a candidate

`AcceptCandidate` · `src/generations.ts:76` · status: **held**

A candidate becomes the next generation only if its second assembly builds Trame's graph as it did and reassembles itself character for character (the fixed point), the laws hold and the older generations still run (or can receive their language); and if it builds Trame's libraries, the example and Trame's graph as the generation in place, whose scenarios hold, unless the differences are declared wanted.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
() => (r: AdvanceReport): boolean =>
    r.secondAsFirst && r.fixedPoint && r.lawsHold && r.olderRun &&
    (r.accepted || (r.scenariosHold && r.librariesAsBefore && r.exampleAsBefore && r.selfAsBefore))
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Refines: [A specification that runs](product.md#ExecutableSpecification)
- Used by: [Advance](commands.md#Advance)
- Applies: [Generations: frozen engines](principles.md#GenerationLayer), [Trame builds Trame](principles.md#TrameBuildsTrame)

<a id="AcceptCandidateCriteria"></a>

**What a candidate needs to be accepted · owner: trame**

| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| A candidate that builds everything as before, reaches its fixed point and keeps the laws is accepted | passed |
| A difference on a library refuses it, unless it is wanted | passed |
| A difference on the example refuses it, unless it is wanted | passed |
| A difference on Trame's graph refuses it, unless it is wanted | passed |
| A scenario that does not hold refuses it, unless the differences are wanted | passed |
| Without a fixed point, nothing is accepted, not even when wanted | passed |
| A second assembly that builds differently refuses it, even when wanted | passed |
| A law that breaks refuses it, even when wanted | passed |
| An older generation that no longer runs, and cannot receive its language, refuses it, even when wanted | passed |

## Decisions

<a id="Advancement"></a>

### What an advance assembles

`Advancement` · `src/generations.ts:50`

The candidate is the component of the engine assembled for the environment of a machine, with the page it writes assembled for the browser: both are compared at the fixed point, and frozen together. Beside the documents of each build, an advance keeps what it printed, in a file of its own, and names what it keeps by whose build it is: the reference (the generation in place), the candidate, the second assembly. The terminal names the first files that differ; the file of differences has them all.

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| component | TrameCli |
| environment | Local |
| page | { component: PageApp, environment: Browser } |
| terminal | terminal.txt |
| saves | { reference: reference, candidate: candidate, second: second } |
| shown | 12 |

- Decided by: trame
- Used by: [Advance](commands.md#Advance), [The fingerprint of an engine](engine.md#EngineFingerprint), [Page resources](platform.md#PageResources)

<a id="EnginePin"></a>

### The engine a project runs

`EnginePin` · `src/generations.ts:127`

A project pins the generation it runs in its configuration (trame.json), under this key: the path of the generation, from the project. Deploying a new generation is moving the pin, which trame advance does when it promotes, for Trame and for the example; going back is moving it back. The launcher (trame.sh) runs the generation the pin names; trame advance takes it as the generation in place.

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| key | engine |

- Decided by: trame
- Rejected: The last generation, whatever it is, a project could neither stay on a generation nor go back to one; An npm package per generation, a registry to publish to, and a version beside the generation's number, for one project today; The candidate, run as it is, an engine that no advance accepted
- Used by: [A project started](command-scenarios.md#ProjectStarted), [Advance](commands.md#Advance), [Start a project](commands.md#Init), [Write the manifest](commands.md#WriteManifest), [Project](engine.md#Project), [The plan of a run elsewhere](shipping.md#ShipmentRunPlan)

<a id="LanguageSharing"></a>

### Generations that share the language

`LanguageSharing` · `src/generations.ts:147`

A generation reaches the repository's language (the prelude, the kinds, the views) through links while it can run on it: it then compiles a project written in the language of today. Each advance replays the oldest and the newest of the other generations that share it on the example, through a view that writes nothing. One that no longer runs lacks what the language now asks, and so do the older ones that share it: each of them, up to the newest that fails, receives the copy of the language archived with the generation in place, the last language they all ran on, with a copy of the example, and runs on its own from then on, as g1 to g8 do; without such an archive, the candidate is refused. Each promotion archives its language, once per fingerprint.

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| oldest | 1 |
| newest | 1 |
| view | index |

- Decided by: trame
- Rejected: A copy of the language in every generation, a generation could then compile only its own graph: it would share no registry with today's projects; Replaying every generation, a minute each, at every advance
- Used by: [Advance](commands.md#Advance)

<a id="Releases"></a>

### Releases of the engine

`Releases` · `src/generations.ts:111`

Each generation frozen is a release of the engine's component: a node of the module releases, named by the prefix and the generation's number. trame advance writes the module at each promotion, from the releases the graph already holds and the one it freezes, so it is never edited by hand; a generation's own release is written after its graph is copied, and is not in its own copy. The value names the module, the kind's constructor and its file, the prefix of a release's name and its owner; the edges a release is written with (ReleaseEdge) and how it reaches its language (LanguageUse) are words of the prelude, which the kind declares.

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| module | releases |
| kind | release |
| prefix | G |
| owner | trame |

- Decided by: trame
- Rejected: The history in the README, written by hand, and it drifted from the generations; A file of records beside the generations, data the graph would not hold, and no view could show
- Used by: [Advance](commands.md#Advance), [Release a version](commands.md#Release), [Records of the releases](#ReleaseRecords)
